images.title: Equal angles in an isosceles trapezium
images.purpose: Shows an isosceles trapezium with a 100° angle: both top angles are 100° and both bottom angles are 80°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large symmetric trapezium in the centre with its parallel sides and equal slanted sides marked and its four angles labelled.
images.exact_structure: One isosceles trapezium in dark outline, symmetric about a vertical line: a long horizontal bottom side and a shorter horizontal top side, each carrying one small dark arrowhead showing they are parallel. The two slanted sides are equal in length and each carries one short tick mark. Angle arcs: at the two top corners teal (#0072B2) arcs, each labelled 100°; at the two bottom corners amber (#E69F00) arcs, each labelled 80°. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In an isosceles trapezium the base angles are equal, and angles along a slanted side add to 180°.
images.description: Shows an isosceles trapezium with a 100° angle: both top angles are 100° and both bottom angles are 80°.
images.context: Practice concept: 180 − 100 = 80; base angles of an isosceles trapezium are equal.

image_decisions.why: The symmetric trapezium with its two angle pairs is the core picture for every trapezium angle question.
